title: Amos Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Amos chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Amos Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Amos Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:1, who are warned with woe?
options: Those at ease in Zion and trusting in the mountain of Samaria
The poor and needy in the land
The priests and Levites in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Those at ease in Zion and trusting in the mountain of Samaria
questions.explanation: Amos 6:1 specifically says, 'Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria.'

questions.question: Which places does Amos 6:2 instruct to visit to compare kingdoms?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:2 says, 'Pass ye unto Calneh, and see; and from thence go ye to Hamath the great: then go down to Gath of the Philistines.'

questions.question: What question is posed in Amos 6:2 about the kingdoms mentioned?
options: Are they better than these kingdoms or their border greater than your border?
Do they worship the true God?
Are their kings just and righteous?
questions.correctAnswer: Are they better than these kingdoms or their border greater than your border?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:2 asks, 'be they better than these kingdoms? or their border greater than your border?'

questions.question: According to Amos 6:3, what do those warned do regarding the evil day?
options: They put far away the evil day and cause the seat of violence to come near
They prepare themselves for the evil day
They warn others about the evil day
questions.correctAnswer: They put far away the evil day and cause the seat of violence to come near
questions.explanation: Amos 6:3 states, 'Ye that put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence to come near;'

questions.question: What luxury is described in Amos 6:4 about those being warned?
options: Lying upon beds of ivory and stretching on couches
Feeding on fish from the sea
questions.correctAnswer: Lying upon beds of ivory and stretching on couches
questions.explanation: Amos 6:4 says, 'That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches...'

questions.question: In Amos 6:4, what animals are mentioned as being eaten by those warned?
options: Lambs out of the flock and calves out of the midst of the stall
questions.correctAnswer: Lambs out of the flock and calves out of the midst of the stall
questions.explanation: Amos 6:4 states, 'and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;'

questions.question: According to Amos 6:5, to what sound do the warned chant?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:5 says, 'That chant to the sound of the viol,'

questions.question: Who is mentioned in Amos 6:5 as an example of inventing musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:5 mentions 'like David' in connection with inventing musical instruments.

questions.question: What do those warned in Amos 6:6 do with wine?
options: They offer wine as a sacrifice
They sell wine in the markets
questions.explanation: Amos 6:6 states, 'That drink wine in bowls,'

questions.question: According to Amos 6:6, what do they anoint themselves with?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:6 says, 'and anoint themselves with the chief ointments;'

questions.question: True or False: Amos 6:7 warns that those who stretch themselves with luxury will have their banquet removed.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:7 states, 'the banquet of them that stretched themselves shall be removed,' warning of judgment on the luxurious.

questions.question: True or False: In Amos 6:8, the LORD says He loves the excellency of Jacob and his palaces.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:8 says, 'I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces,' indicating God's disapproval.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 6:9 describes a situation where if ten men remain in one house, they shall die.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:9 states, 'if there remain ten men in one house, that they shall die.'

questions.question: True or False: Amos 6:10 shows that people will freely mention the name of the LORD during destruction.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:10 says, 'Hold thy tongue: for we may not make mention of the name of the LORD,' indicating silence.

questions.question: In Amos 6, which instruction comes first?
options: To pass unto Calneh and see
To anoint themselves with chief ointments
To lie upon beds of ivory
questions.correctAnswer: To pass unto Calneh and see
questions.explanation: Amos 6:2 says first to 'Pass ye unto Calneh, and see;' which comes before other descriptions of luxury in verses 4-6.

medium.title: Amos Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Amos Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:6, what is the attitude of those who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with ointments toward the affliction of Joseph?
options: They are indifferent and not grieved
questions.correctAnswer: They are indifferent and not grieved
questions.explanation: Amos 6:6 states that these people 'drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph,' showing their indifference toward suffering.

questions.question: What consequence does Amos 6:7 give for those who stretch themselves in ease and are not grieved for Joseph's affliction?
options: They will be praised by the nations
They shall go captive with the first that go captive
questions.correctAnswer: They shall go captive with the first that go captive
questions.explanation: Amos 6:7 explains that those who live in luxury without concern will 'go captive with the first that go captive,' indicating judgment upon their complacency.

questions.question: How does Amos 6:8 describe God's feelings toward the excellency of Jacob and his palaces?
questions.explanation: In Amos 6:8, God says, 'I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces,' showing divine displeasure toward their pride and complacency.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:9, what will happen if ten men remain in one house?
options: They shall be protected by God
questions.explanation: Amos 6:9 warns that even if ten men remain in one house, 'they shall die,' emphasizing the severity of coming judgment.

questions.question: In Amos 6:10, why do the survivors say 'Hold thy tongue' and avoid mentioning the name of the LORD?
options: Because they are in mourning and despair
questions.explanation: Amos 6:10 explains that they say 'Hold thy tongue: for we may not make mention of the name of the LORD,' indicating a divine command to silence during judgment.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:11 say the LORD will do to both the great and little houses?
options: He will bless them with peace
He will smite them with breaches and clefts
He will protect them from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He will smite them with breaches and clefts
questions.explanation: Amos 6:11 states that the LORD commands to 'smite the great house with breaches, and the little house with clefts,' signifying thorough destruction.

questions.question: Amos 6:12 uses a metaphor involving horses running upon the rock and plowing with oxen. What sin is this metaphor illustrating?
options: Turning judgment into gall and righteousness into hemlock
questions.correctAnswer: Turning judgment into gall and righteousness into hemlock
questions.explanation: Amos 6:12 asks if horses will run on rock or oxen plow there, then states they have 'turned judgment into gall, and the fruit of righteousness into hemlock,' illustrating their perversion of justice.

questions.question: What false confidence is rebuked in Amos 6:13?
options: Boasting in their own strength and power
questions.correctAnswer: Boasting in their own strength and power
questions.explanation: Amos 6:13 rebukes those who 'say, Have we not taken to us horns by our own strength?' exposing their arrogant self-reliance.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:14 say God will do in response to the arrogance described in earlier verses?
options: Raise up a nation to afflict Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Raise up a nation to afflict Israel
questions.explanation: Amos 6:14 declares that God will 'raise up against you a nation... and they shall afflict you,' as judgment for their pride and unrepentance.

questions.question: How does Amos 6:6-7 connect the luxurious lifestyle to the coming captivity?
options: Their luxury will protect them from captivity
Their disregard for Joseph's affliction causes them to go captive with the first captives
Their music and wine will comfort them in captivity
Their wealth will buy their freedom
questions.correctAnswer: Their disregard for Joseph's affliction causes them to go captive with the first captives
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 link the indulgent lifestyle and lack of grief for Joseph’s suffering with the consequence of going captive, showing cause and effect.

questions.question: Based on Amos 6:9-10, what is the significance of the inquiry 'Is there yet any with thee?' during the time of judgment?
options: It reflects the thoroughness of death and the silence about the LORD’s name
It signals the start of a feast
It indicates a gathering for worship
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the thoroughness of death and the silence about the LORD’s name
questions.explanation: Amos 6:9-10 depict a scene of death where survivors check if anyone remains and then silence is commanded regarding the LORD’s name, symbolizing complete devastation and fear.

questions.question: True or False? Amos 6:8 declares that God will protect the city and its inhabitants because of their palaces.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:8 states that God 'abhors the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces' and will 'deliver up the city with all that is therein,' indicating judgment, not protection.

questions.question: True or False? Amos 6:11 teaches that both large and small households will be affected by the LORD’s judgment.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:11 says the LORD will smite both 'the great house with breaches, and the little house with clefts,' showing that judgment is comprehensive.

questions.question: True or False? Amos 6:14 offers a promise of restoration and blessing to Israel after their affliction.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:14 predicts that God will raise a nation against Israel to afflict them, emphasizing judgment rather than restoration.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles with pride and self-reliance. Based on Amos 6, what biblical truth applies?
options: God rewards those who trust in their own strength
Pride leads to judgment as God raises adversaries against the arrogant
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to judgment as God raises adversaries against the arrogant
questions.explanation: Amos 6:13-14 rebuke boasting in one’s own strength and warn that God will raise a nation to afflict Israel because of their pride and arrogance.

hard.title: Amos Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Amos Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:11, what will the LORD do to the great house and the little house?
options: Smite the great house with breaches and the little house with clefts
Bless both houses with peace and prosperity
Ignore the houses and punish the surrounding nations
Restore the houses to their former glory
questions.correctAnswer: Smite the great house with breaches and the little house with clefts
questions.explanation: Amos 6:11 states that the LORD will command and smite the great house with breaches and the little house with clefts, signaling judgment on all levels of society.

questions.question: In Amos 6:12, what metaphor is used to describe the turning of judgment into gall and righteousness into hemlock?
options: Horses running upon the rock and oxen plowing there
questions.correctAnswer: Horses running upon the rock and oxen plowing there
questions.explanation: Amos 6:12 uses the metaphor of horses running on rock and oxen plowing there to illustrate the futility and unnaturalness of turning judgment into gall and righteousness into hemlock.

questions.question: Who does Amos 6:13 describe as rejoicing in a thing of nought and claiming strength by their own horns?
options: Those who boast in their own strength and achievements
questions.correctAnswer: Those who boast in their own strength and achievements
questions.explanation: Amos 6:13 criticizes those who rejoice in something worthless and arrogantly claim strength by their own horns, a metaphor for self-reliance and pride.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:14 prophesy that the LORD will do against the house of Israel?
options: Raise up a nation to afflict them from Hemath to the river of the wilderness
Send a prophet to restore them
Bless them with abundance and peace
Divide their land among neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: Raise up a nation to afflict them from Hemath to the river of the wilderness
questions.explanation: Amos 6:14 prophesies that the LORD will raise up a nation to afflict Israel over a wide territory, signaling impending judgment and exile.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'Hold thy tongue: for we may not make mention of the name of the LORD' in Amos 6:10?
options: It reflects a time of such devastation that even God's name is feared to be spoken
It encourages loud praise of God in times of suffering
It forbids the use of God's name in worship
It indicates reverence through silence in holy places
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects a time of such devastation that even God's name is feared to be spoken
questions.explanation: Amos 6:10 shows the extreme fear and desolation during judgment when people dare not mention the LORD's name, indicating deep distress and reverence.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God raising up a nation to judge Israel, similar to Amos 6:14?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:6 describes the Assyrian conquest and exile of Israel, fulfilling the judgment foretold in Amos 6:14.

questions.question: In Amos 6:7, what is said will happen to those who stretch themselves and feast without concern?
options: They shall go captive with the first that go captive, and their banquet shall be removed
They shall be rewarded with lasting peace
They shall be honored by all nations
questions.correctAnswer: They shall go captive with the first that go captive, and their banquet shall be removed
questions.explanation: Amos 6:7 warns that those indulging in luxury will face captivity alongside the first captives, losing their pleasures as a consequence of their complacency.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'gall' in Amos 6:12 literally mean, and how does it relate to the verse's meaning?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'gall' (מרור, maror) means bitter poison, illustrating how judgment has been corrupted and made harmful, as described in Amos 6:12.

questions.question: Amos 6:4 describes certain people 'that lie upon beds of ivory.' What does this image primarily symbolize?
options: Luxury and complacency among Israel's elite
questions.correctAnswer: Luxury and complacency among Israel's elite
questions.explanation: Amos 6:4 uses the image of lying on ivory beds to depict the wealthy elite indulging in comfort while neglecting justice.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily employed in Amos 6:12 when comparing horses running upon the rock to the corruption of justice?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:12 uses metaphor to compare the unnatural act of horses running on rock with the unnatural corruption of justice.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:8, why does the LORD abhor the excellency of Jacob and hate his palaces?
options: Because of Israel's pride and injustice leading to judgment
Because the palaces were poorly built
Because the people refused to fight in wars
questions.correctAnswer: Because of Israel's pride and injustice leading to judgment
questions.explanation: Amos 6:8 indicates God's abhorrence of Jacob's pride and palatial luxury, which symbolize injustice and lead to divine judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 6:9 predicts that if ten men remain in one house, they will all survive the coming judgment.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:9 states that if ten men remain in one house, they shall die, indicating the severity of the judgment.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains similar warnings about luxury and complacency leading to downfall, as seen in Amos 6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah contains similar warnings against complacency and luxury leading to judgment, which parallels themes in Amos 6.

questions.question: Who are the 'chief ointments' users mentioned in Amos 6:6, and what does this signify culturally?
options: The wealthy elite indulging in luxury and self-care
The priests preparing for temple duties
questions.correctAnswer: The wealthy elite indulging in luxury and self-care
questions.explanation: Amos 6:6 highlights the rich who anoint themselves with expensive ointments, symbolizing their self-indulgence and neglect of social justice.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'Have we not taken to us horns by our own strength?' in Amos 6:13 reflects a humility before God.
questions.explanation: Amos 6:13 reveals arrogance and pride in human strength, not humility, as the people boast in their own power symbolized by 'horns.'

theological.title: Amos Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Amos Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:1 warn against regarding those in Zion?
options: Woe to them that are at ease
questions.correctAnswer: Woe to them that are at ease
questions.explanation: Amos 6:1 specifically states, 'Woe to them that are at ease in Zion,' indicating a warning against complacency and false security.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:3, what do the people do regarding the 'evil day'?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:3 states, 'Ye that put far away the evil day,' highlighting the people's denial of impending judgment.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:8 reveal about God's feelings toward the 'excellency of Jacob'?
questions.explanation: In Amos 6:8, God declares, 'I abhor the excellency of Jacob,' indicating His disdain for the pride of Israel.

questions.question: What will happen to those who are complacent, according to Amos 6:7?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:7 states, 'Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive,' indicating the consequence of their complacency.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:12 suggest about the people's actions towards justice?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:12 says, 'for ye have turned judgment into gall,' indicating a perversion of justice among the people.

questions.question: According to Amos 6:10, what will happen if ten men remain in one house?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:9 states, 'that they shall die,' indicating the severity of judgment that will fall upon the people.

questions.question: How does Amos 6:4 describe the lifestyles of the wealthy?
options: They lie on beds of ivory
questions.correctAnswer: They lie on beds of ivory
questions.explanation: Amos 6:4 describes the wealthy as those 'that lie upon beds of ivory,' emphasizing their luxury and indulgence.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:13 imply about the nation's pride?
options: They have taken horns by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: They have taken horns by their own strength
questions.explanation: Amos 6:13 indicates pride in their accomplishments, stating, 'which say, Have we not taken to us horns by our own strength?'

questions.question: What does Amos 6:5 suggest about the people's attitude towards music?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:5 describes the people as 'That chant to the sound of the viol, and invent to themselves instruments of musick,' indicating a focus on entertainment.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Amos 6:1 and Amos 6:8 convey about Israel's security?
options: They are safe in their wealth
They are secure in God's favor
questions.explanation: Amos 6:1 warns against complacency in Zion, while 6:8 shows that God abhors their pride, indicating that their security is false and leads to judgment.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:14 indicate about the future of Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:14 states that God will raise up a nation against Israel that will afflict them, indicating a future of suffering.

questions.question: What does Amos 6:6 reveal about the people's reaction to Joseph's affliction?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:6 states, 'but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph,' demonstrating their lack of compassion.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be derived from Amos 6:11 and Amos 6:12 regarding justice?
options: Justice must be upheld at all costs
Judgment is perverted and justice is neglected
Justice is only for the rich
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment is perverted and justice is neglected
questions.explanation: Amos 6:11 speaks of God's judgment on houses, while 6:12 discusses how the people have turned judgment into gall, indicating a neglect of true justice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Old Testament God is indifferent to human suffering. What does Amos 6:6-7 actually teach?
options: God is indifferent to all suffering
God cares only for the rich
God is concerned about Israel's affliction
questions.correctAnswer: God is concerned about Israel's affliction
questions.explanation: Amos 6:6 shows that God is aware of Joseph's affliction, and in 6:7, the consequences of complacency indicate God's active judgment on the people’s indifference to suffering.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Amos 6:8 regarding His relationship with Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos 6:8 reveals God's justice as He declares that He abhors the pride of Israel, indicating that He will not overlook their sins.
